clue.text: Design one's entered for patent

indicators.note: one piece has entered the other, so it sits inside the word for design

parts.note: a design is a plan
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone has filed a design to get a patent on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patent' looks like a noun about inventions, but here it is the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something patent is obvious, open to view, as something clear and evident is.

clue.text: Briefly visit religious leader, mostly at home

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word for the leader is kept, its final letter lost

parts.note: the Pope leads the Catholic Church
at home means in

explanation.surface: A quick call on a church leader who is usually at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop by somewhere for a short, casual call is a common idiom.

clue.text: Plastic train from US

explanation.surface: A credit card is a train of thought from America.
explanation.definitionFit: The credit card company is a byword for plastic money, and a fast train in America could be called this too.

clue.text: Guy involved in prank? Yes, or snooper

indicators.note: the letters are tangled up together, so the words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A man caught up in a practical joke turns out to be a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' signals the anagram of PRANK YES OR; 'Guy' is a link here, adding colour to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A busybody who pries into other people's affairs is the idiom for a snooper.

clue.text: What you're doing could be bother!

explanation.surface: Solving this puzzle might be a nuisance!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bother!' is a mild curse, so it is an angry word.
explanation.definitionFit: The solver is busy with a puzzle of clues and grid, and an irritable exclamation is an angry word.

clue.text: Liberal accepted by enchanting female's coterie

indicators.note: one piece is taken in by the other, so the abbreviation goes inside the name

parts.note: Circe is the enchantress of Greek myth who turned men into swine

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is welcomed into a charming woman's set.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is an exclusive group of people, a select set.

clue.text: Happening to get caught as one breaks into old study

indicators.note: the letters force their way inside the word for study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A burglar is caught breaking into an old study.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion is an event, something that takes place.

clue.text: Thus having to accept full house? No, beat it!

indicators.note: the word for thus takes in the other piece inside it

parts.note: so means thus
HO is an abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Thus taking on a winning poker hand? No, get lost!
explanation.walkthrough: 'full house' looks like poker, but it just gives an abbreviation for house.
explanation.definitionFit: A word said to drive away an animal or person, telling them to go away.

clue.text: Basis of political power of general with lower rank

parts.note: overall means general, comprehensive
majority is the rank of a major, below a general

explanation.surface: A general and his junior officer hold the reins of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like an army officer but means comprehensive; 'lower rank' is then the rank of major, below general.
explanation.definitionFit: A government with more seats than all other parties combined can pass its laws.

clue.text: Turned red, perhaps, about one's honour being violated

indicators.note: the word for coloured is placed around the other letters

parts.note: dyed red is one example of a dyed colour
one is I; the 's is 'is', giving IS
an OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: Someone blushes about the way their honour has been violated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned red' suggests blushing, but means coloured with dye.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule or order that is broken has been flouted, not obeyed.

clue.text: They prepare fast food from certain fruit found in cupboard

indicators.note: the letters are discovered inside the word for cupboard

parts.note: a press is a cupboard, especially for linen
sure means certain
a cooker is a cooking apple

explanation.surface: A kitchen tip on making quick meals from fruit kept in the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast food' is not takeaways but food cooked quickly under steam pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealed pans that cook food quickly under steam pressure are kitchen appliances.

clue.text: Form of digital enhancement applied to catch European type

parts.note: to nail someone is to catch them
Polish describes someone from Poland

explanation.surface: A digital upgrade that helps to catch a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' sounds like computing, but it means of the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnish applied to fingernails makes the fingers look better.

clue.text: Horse that's said to be malicious

explanation.surface: A horse with a reputation for nastiness.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barb is a North African breed of horse, and a cutting remark is a spiteful thing to say.

clue.text: Details of two-way movements

explanation.surface: The particulars of movements going both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The intricate particulars of something are an idiom, and comings and goings are literally movements in and out.

clue.text: Scholarly positions found in dailies, including Independent

indicators.note: the word for cleaners takes the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a daily or char is a cleaning lady, so dailies are chars

explanation.surface: Academic jobs are advertised in the papers, including this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dailies' looks like newspapers, but is British slang for cleaners, called chars.
explanation.definitionFit: A professorship is called a chair at a university.

clue.text: Understate significance of sad drama

parts.note: down means sad
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: Playing down how important a gloomy play is.
explanation.definitionFit: To minimise or make light of something is to make it seem less important.

clue.text: Part of sketch presented in full — and the rest

indicators.note: part of means a short run of letters is taken from the word sketch

parts.note: the abbreviation taken from sketch is written out in full, adding these letters

explanation.surface: A section of a drawing shown complete, and the remainder too.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ETC lies in 'sketch'; 'presented in full' expands that abbreviation into the full Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used to mean and so on, and other things.

clue.text: Result of fixing broken clutch that's taken a beating

definitions.text: Result of fixing broken clutch that's taken a beating

parts.words: Result of fixing broken clutch that's taken a beating
parts.note: a clutch is a set of eggs; once broken and beaten, then cooked, they make a dish

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests mending a car's clutch, but the clutch is a batch of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of beaten eggs cooked in a pan describes it exactly.

clue.text: Club, perhaps, concealing an unfounded rumour

indicators.note: the word for club hides the other letters inside it

parts.note: a club is a playing card suit, so a card

explanation.surface: A club is hiding a baseless piece of gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is a false report or hoax.

clue.text: Problem in murder case for Holloway recorder

explanation.surface: A tricky murder case for someone keeping notes in Holloway.
explanation.walkthrough: Holloway is a district of north London, and 'The Diary of a Nobody' is a Victorian comic novel whose diarist, Charles Pooter, lives there.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a corpse a murder is hard to prove, and Pooter is the diarist of a famous comic novel.

clue.text: Part of race with extra pressure for Northerner

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a race
P is the abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: A runner from the far north needs extra push for a stage of the race.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sami people of far northern Scandinavia were long called by this name.

clue.text: Slightly mistimed call before fighting resumes

explanation.surface: A slightly late call before a boxing match restarts.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wrong by a few moments is a plain reading, and a boxing referee's announcement before each round is the other.

clue.text: Trace elements, metal and semimetal, one symbolised

parts.note: tin is a metal
germanium is a semimetal whose chemical symbol is Ge

explanation.surface: A chemistry note on trace elements found in metals and semimetals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trace elements' looks like one phrase but splits: 'Trace' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight hint or touch of something, as in a faint colour.

clue.text: Fascinated by headless horse

indicators.note: headless means the first letter of the horse word is removed

parts.note: a pinto is a piebald horse

explanation.surface: Someone captivated by a horse with no head.
explanation.definitionFit: Being keen on or enthusiastic about something is a colloquial sense.

clue.text: Volunteer could be involved with Gore in this

definitions.text: Volunteer could be involved with Gore in this

indicators.note: involved means twisted together, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Al Gore and a volunteer might be part of this environmental movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes VOLUNTEER, GORE and IN together.
explanation.definitionFit: The farming boom of high-yield crops in the 1960s is the historic sense; Gore is a green campaigner.

clue.text: Army scout given new order, as usual

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An army scout receives fresh orders, as is routine.
explanation.definitionFit: What is customary is habitual, the normal practice.

clue.text: Fashion writer

explanation.surface: A fashion writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode or trend is a fashion, and a stylus or pointed instrument for writing on wax is an old meaning.
